newsitem.title: USA: Brady debt slips, spreads over US Treasuries widen.
newsitem.headline: Brady debt slips, spreads over US Treasuries widen.

text.p: Emerging market debt prices slipped in light trading, with yield spreads widening for many issues as U.S. Treasuries recorded smaller declines, traders said on Monday.
"We're just down tracking Treasuries," one Brady bond trader said. "Very little has moved today, in terms of customer flows."
Yield spreads for the three largest Latin American economies -- Argentina, Brazil and Mexico -- gave a mixed performance.
Argentina FRBs were unchanged at 95-1/4 bid, shaving five basis points off their spread, while Brazil "C" bonds dipped 1/4 to 83 bid, their spread increasing by one basis point.
Mexico discounts tightened modestly as their price rose 1/8 to 94-5/8, but the country's global '26 widened three basis points as its price dipped 5/8 to 120-1/4.
Going forward, spreads should hold fairly steady absent a shock to the U.S. Treasury market, said Dan Peirce, chief emerging markets strategist at Bank of Boston.
"My view would be unless the Treasury market really sustains some serious damage ... spreads are going to hold out all right," Peirce said.
He quantified "serious damage" as a rapid backup in the 30-year bond yield to about 6.75 percent from its current level near 6.5 percent.
Elsewhere, the confirmation of Ecuador's new finance minister, Marco Flores, had little effect on the country's Brady bonds, traders said. Ecuador Pars fell 5/8 to 53-3/8, widening four basis points.
"I take that as good news, but the market won't make much of it," one trader said of the Flores announcement.
